title: Browse All Corporate Departments
description_markdown: Write a query to retrieve all columns and rows from the `departments` table to examine corporate divisions.
starter_query:
-- Select all columns from departments
SELECT * FROM ...
solution_query: SELECT dept_id, dept_name, location, budget FROM departments;
solution_explanation: The SELECT statement specifies which columns to retrieve from the `departments` table.
common_mistakes: Misspelling the table name as 'department' instead of 'departments'.
interview_tip: In production APIs, prefer explicit column names over SELECT * to prevent schema coupling.
hints: Use the SELECT keyword followed by the table columns or asterisk.
Specify FROM departments to identify the source table.
The full statement is: SELECT dept_id, dept_name, location, budget FROM departments;

title: Calculate Unit Profit Margins on Merchandise
description_markdown: Calculate the gross unit profit for every product by subtracting `cost` from `price` as `unit_profit`. Return `product_name`, `price`, `cost`, and `unit_profit`.
solution_query: SELECT product_name, price, cost, (price - cost) AS unit_profit FROM products;
solution_explanation: Applies column subtraction arithmetic in the SELECT projection list to compute unit profit.
common_mistakes: Subtracting price from cost instead of cost from price.
interview_tip: Arithmetic in SELECT evaluates row-by-row on the fly without altering stored table values.
hints: Select product_name, price, cost as well.
Query: SELECT product_name, price, cost, (price - cost) AS unit_profit FROM products;

title: Model Five Percent Compensation Merit Increase
description_markdown: For each employee in `employees`, project a 5% salary increase (`salary * 1.05`) as `projected_salary`. Return `first_name`, `last_name`, `salary`, and `projected_salary`.
solution_query: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary, (salary * 1.05) AS projected_salary FROM employees;
solution_explanation: Multiplies current salary by 1.05 to calculate the increased total compensation.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by 0.05 which gives only the raise increment rather than the full projected salary.
hints: Multiply salary by 1.05 to get the new total: `(salary * 1.05) AS projected_salary`.
Query: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary, (salary * 1.05) AS projected_salary FROM employees;

hints: Query: SELECT first_name, last_name, gpa, (gpa * 25.0) AS scaled_points FROM students;

solution_query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, (reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) AS reorder_gap FROM stock_items;
solution_explanation: Subtracts current quantity from threshold level to determine reorder urgency gap.
hints: Query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, (reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) AS reorder_gap FROM stock_items;
